messages.subject: Matt trick with crossed random effects
parts:
Hi guys, I am trying to apply the Matt Trick in the context of crossed random effects (states i in I and years j in J), with a model like that shown below:

    y = B_0 + <other predictors> + B_State_i + B_Year_j

The code below is based on the various examples in the manual and FAQ, except that the random effects (B_State and B_Year) are centered at zero (with an intercept included in the model) rather than at the overall mean. I just wanted to check that I am not missing out on the benefits of the reparameterization through this set up. If so, I assume the approach would be to center one of the random effects at the overall mean (and remove the intercept term).

Thanks - Nick

parameters {  
  vector e_B_State[I];         // standardized errors in State random effects 
  vector e_B_Year[J];          // standardized errors in Year random effects
  vector B_0;                  // intercept
  real<lower=0> sigState;      // Std dev of state random effects
  real<lower=0> SigYear;       // Std dev of year random effects
  // some other betas....
}
transformed parameters {
  vector B_State[I];         // State random effects
  vector B_Year[J];          // Year random effects
  B_State[I] <- e_B_State[I]*sigState;
  B_Year[J]  <- e_B_Year[J]*sigYear;
}
model {
  e_B_State ~ normal(0.0, 1.0); // implies B_State ~ normal(0.0,sigState)
  e_B_Year  ~ normal(0.0, 1.0); // implies B_Year  ~ normal(0.0,sigYear)
  sigState  ~ cauchy(0.0, 5.0);  // Std dev of state random effects
  sigYear   ~ cauchy(0.0, 5.0);  // Std dev of year random effects
  // likelihood as a function of B_0, B_State, B_Year, and the other betas
}

> B_Year) are centered at zero (with an intercept included in the model) rather than at the overall mean. I just wanted to
> check that I am not missing out on the benefits of the reparameterization through this set up.

The idea's just to decouple the parameters from
the data in the prior. You see that in your model.

> If so, I assume the
> approach would be to center one of the random effects at the overall mean (and remove the intercept term).

Other way around. That is, like you have it below.

The Matt trick creates the uncentered parameterization.
So all the sampling statements have 0 means or locations.

Of course, your model won't compile because it's the
wrong vector syntax. :-)

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: l'esprit de l'escalier and confessional debugging
parts:
On 10/6/13 9:31 PM, Nick Menzies wrote:
> Hi Bob's -- thanks for the quick response. Yes, things not quite right in the parameter declarations -- I haven't got to
> the point where I just see these errors as I type them (but rather just after I send off the email...).

Unfortunately, my mistakes often make it all the way through to
the manual :-(

As to seeing errors just after hitting send, I think we need
a term for the e-mail equivalent of "l'esprit de l'escalier."

I did add a section talking about the "rubber ducky" phenomenon
for debugging in the intro for the new manual:

http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rubber_duck_debugging

I sort of like McConnell's term "confessional debugging," because
that's what it often feels like when you're sort of embarrassed
by the code you wrote.

- Bob
